reason: Structural difference. Figma has one variable with 10 modes; CSS has ten --icon-color-<mode> tokens. Verified equal.

name: Lightbox backdrop blur
reason: Equivalent rendering: the Figma blur radius is double the CSS blur radius, so Figma 12 is CSS blur(6px) (Figma's own code export gives blur(6px)). Source: Figma forum answers on blur in Dev Mode, not the official docs. No blur token matches, so the value is a literal.

Structural difference (D-49). There is no Figma variable: Figma reads a numeric variable bound to line height or letter spacing as pixels, so it cannot hold a percentage. The canonical value lives in the text styles (docs/data/figma-text-styles.json) and the percentage equals the CSS value after unit conversion. Revisit when Figma supports percentages in variables: create variables with these names and bind the styles; the CSS stays the same.

name: Compact UI text at 140%
reason: Short UI text (labels, captions, links, names) was designed denser than running text; the difference to Figma is 2.6 px per line at 13px. Revisit if a Figma component needs this text. (D-52)

name: Airy body text at 170%
reason: Running text in cards and lists was designed more open; 170% already exists as a Figma value for Body lg and Body xl, and forcing 160% shortens pages by 10 to 78 px. Revisit if a Figma component needs this text. (D-52)

name: Small secondary text at 11px with positive tracking
reason: Intentional small secondary text. It is not uppercase, so it does not use --ls-widest (D-46 reserves 12% for uppercase labels of up to three words). (D-52)

name: Waiting for the auth gate
reason: Not rendered on any shipped page: no shipped page loads js/auth.js, and .experience-item__logo-mono has no instance. Pending, not accepted; revisit when the gate ships (D-52)
